analysis.investment_thesis: Exim Routes is a tiny, 6-year-old paper recycling trader with spectacular revenue growth (134% CAGR) but zero cash generation — a fatal flaw for a commodity middleman with no moat. At 37.5x P/E with INR 248 Cr market cap and chronically negative OCF, the market is pricing in a business quality that does not exist.
key_strengths: Revenue has scaled from INR 4 Cr (2021) to INR 121 Cr (2025) — execution speed is real
ROCE of 55% and ROE of 54% look impressive, reflecting asset-light trading model on a small equity base
Promoter holding stable at 52.44% with FII/DII participation providing some institutional validation
key_risks: Profit-to-cash disconnect is alarming: INR 8 Cr net profit in 2025 but OCF of -5 Cr and FCF of -9 Cr — 0/5 years of positive operating cash flow signals aggressive revenue recognition or working capital trap
Zero moat: paper recycling facilitation is a pure commodity trading model, easily replicated by any well-capitalised trader with supplier/mill relationships
Overvalued at 37.5x P/E for a business with INR 121 Cr revenue, no cash generation, and no durable competitive advantage in a thin-margin sector
red_flags: OCF negative every single year (-5 Cr in FY25) while reporting INR 8 Cr net profit — classic earnings quality red flag
Total assets ballooned from INR 21 Cr to INR 54 Cr in one year, funded mostly by IPO equity (INR 25 Cr) and borrowings (INR 9 Cr), not organic cash generation
Incorporated only in April 2019 — no tested business cycle experience; entire track record is during a bull run in commodity volumes
Paper & paper products is a structurally weak sector — no government PLI tailwind, no consumption upgrade story, no pricing power for a middleman
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From where I sit, the first thing I check in any business is whether profits convert to cash — and Exim Routes fails this test comprehensively. They reported INR 8 Cr net profit in FY25, but operating cash flow was negative INR 5 Cr and free cash flow was negative INR 9 Cr. This gap, repeated across every single year (0/5 years positive OCF), tells me that revenue is being booked before cash is collected, or working capital is being stuffed into the supply chain. In a commodity trading business, this is deeply worrying — these businesses must turn inventory and receivables fast, or they destroy value.

The business model itself offers no reason for long-term ownership. Exim Routes is a platform that connects recycled paper suppliers to Indian paper mills. There is no technology barrier, no brand, no switching cost, and no regulatory protection. Any paper mill can source directly; any well-funded trader can replicate this model. The 134% revenue CAGR from a INR 4 Cr base is impressive optically but tells us more about the starting point than about durable competitive advantage. At 37.5x P/E for a commodity facilitation business generating negative free cash, the market is pricing in a story that the fundamentals do not support. I would rather sit on cash than own this.
